title: Horchata
subtitle: Mexican rice and cinnamon drink, served cold
excerpt: Horchata is a cold, milky-looking drink made from blended rice, cinnamon and sugar. It needs 8 hours to soak but takes only 10 minutes of active work. It is sweet, cooling and slightly spiced.
sourceNotes: Horchata arrived in Mexico via Spain, where a similar drink made from tiger nuts (chufa) is popular in Valencia. Mexican horchata swapped tiger nuts for rice and became a staple drink at taquerias and family meals across the country. It is often served alongside spicy food as a cooling counterpoint.

recipe.batchNotes: Scales well. Make a double batch and keep in a large jug in the fridge for up to 3 days.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Soak the rice and cinnamon overnight. Blend, strain and chill before serving.

content.text: This recipe makes 6 glasses and takes 10 minutes of active preparation plus 8 hours of soaking time. The rinsed rice and cinnamon sticks soak overnight in 1 litre of cold water. The next day the mixture is blended with a further 1 litre of fresh cold water, strained through a fine sieve and sweetened with sugar. Serve over ice, with a drop of vanilla extract if you like.

The straining step is important. A fine mesh sieve lined with a piece of muslin or a clean tea towel gives the cleanest result. If you only have a coarse sieve, pass the liquid through it twice. The finished drink should look milky white with no gritty texture. Stir the jug before pouring each glass as the rice starch will settle to the bottom.

Rinse the rice well under cold water until the water runs clear. Place it in a large bowl or jug with the 2 cinnamon sticks. Pour over 1 litre of cold water. Cover and leave to soak for at least 8 hours, or overnight in the fridge.
Pour the soaked rice, cinnamon sticks and soaking water into a blender. Add a further 1 litre of fresh cold water. Blend on high for 2 minutes until as smooth as possible.

Set a fine mesh sieve over a large jug or bowl. Pour the blended mixture through the sieve in batches. Press the rice pulp gently with the back of a spoon to extract as much liquid as possible. Discard the pulp and cinnamon sticks.
Stir the sugar into the strained liquid until fully dissolved. Taste and add more sugar if you prefer it sweeter. Add a few drops of vanilla extract if using.
Chill in the fridge until very cold, at least 1 hour. Stir the jug before pouring. Serve over plenty of ice.

attrs.symptom: The drink has a gritty texture even after straining
attrs.cause: The sieve was not fine enough to catch all the rice particles
attrs.fix: Line the sieve with a piece of muslin or a very clean, thin tea towel. Pour the mixture through slowly. For the smoothest result, strain twice through a fine sieve. The texture should be completely smooth with no graininess.

attrs.symptom: The horchata separates quickly and looks watery on top
attrs.cause: Rice starch naturally settles as it sits
attrs.fix: This is normal. Stir or shake the jug thoroughly before every pour. The drink will not last more than 3 days in the fridge before the starch breaks down and the flavour fades.

attrs.symptom: The cinnamon flavour is very weak
attrs.cause: The cinnamon sticks were not broken before soaking, limiting the surface area
attrs.fix: Snap each cinnamon stick into 3 or 4 pieces before adding to the soaking water. This exposes more of the interior and releases more flavour during the long soak.

content.text: Horchata is the drink of the taqueria. You find it in big glass jars on the counter at taco stands across Mexico, alongside agua de jamaica and tamarind water. Families make it at home for weekend meals. It is mild and sweet, which makes it popular with children and a natural match for chilli-heavy food.
